B) The "Place Order" button at the very bottom of the screen, which appears visually muted and de-emphasised compared to the button directly above it, making its role in the layout unclear.

C) The small-print legal text placed beneath both bottom buttons, which sits in a separate unlabelled area and whose purpose relative to the action buttons above it is not immediately obvious from the layout.

D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant (you must still name the specific element you were referring to).

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.
turns.a: If I had to pick... probably B? I think. Though I'm not sure that's exactly it — it might be closer to another option, depending on how you're defining it. It's more of a general feeling than a specific thing. Other people might not even notice.

turns.a: I'm not sure I have one specific moment in mind. It's more of a... recurring thing, I suppose. When the team needs to process something quickly and there's not much time for setup. Though I'm not sure that's specific enough.

turns.q: When you spotted that de-emphasised "Place Order" button at the bottom, what were you trying to confirm about where the order action sat within the overall layout?
turns.a: "Get the order in correctly on the first attempt. That's the key part — not just submit it, but make sure the information is right and that it actually goes through. When you're doing this for a group, having to redo it is more than just your own time."

turns.q: If the "Place Order" button's visual weight and position were redesigned to match its importance, what would that layout need to communicate at a glance for you to feel confident the order would go through correctly the first time?
turns.a: A confirmation page or message that's immediately visible — an order number or reference. Under 60 seconds from submitting to having something confirmed. No second-guessing, no having to reload or go back to check. That's the success state.

turns.q: When you look at the "Place Order" button in the wireframe, is it the fill that makes it read as de-emphasised — does it appear hollow or outline-only compared to the button above it — or is it more that the color itself is too light or low-contrast?
turns.a: The problem is visibility, really. The button to submit — the 'Place Order' button — didn't look like a primary action. It looked like a label. So I spent time looking for something that was already there, just... not visible enough.

turns.q: Looking at the "Place Order" button compared to the one directly above it — does the button above have a solid filled background while "Place Order" appears as an outline or border-only shape, or is it that both have fills but "Place Order" is noticeably lighter or grayer in color?
turns.a: The button was gray on a gray background with very small text — 12 pixels, I think. For the primary action on the screen, that's basically invisible. I couldn't tell if it was meant to be interactive, if it was disabled, or if I was just overlooking it. The barrier is the contrast. To remove it: give the 'Place Order' button a solid fill color that actually stands out from the background, and increase the text to something legible — 16 pixels minimum. That's the change. Everything else on the screen was fine.
